blurb: Standard anatomical position on the anterior female figure: thoracic, abdominal, pelvic, and limb surface landmarks connected to deeper organ systems.
lead: Surface anatomy bridges what we see on the living body with what lies beneath, linking palpable skeletal landmarks to thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic organs. In this illustrated guide to female body surface anatomy, we examine 20 documented structures—including brain, thyroid gland, lungs, heart—linking regional topography, tissue architecture, physiological mechanisms, and clinical reasoning.
overview: Surface anatomy bridges what we see on the living body with what lies beneath, linking palpable skeletal landmarks to thoracic, abdominal, and pelvic organs. Use this page as an orientation map: click any glowing organ to jump into its full entry with the realistic render, labelled schematic and quiz. Within the human body, the female body — anterior (Corpus femininum) is situated in whole body — anterior view, receives arterial perfusion via systemic + pulmonary circuits, and is innervated by central + peripheral nervous systems.

The brain (Encephalon) control centre housed in the skull, glowing through the translucent scalp. Physiologically, the brain integrates sensation, movement, thought, memory and autonomic drive. Structurally, the thyroid gland (Glandula thyroidea) comprises butterfly-shaped gland on the front of the neck. Physiologically, the thyroid gland governs sets metabolic rate via T3/T4 under TSH control. The lungs (Pulmones) are paired thoracic organs flanking the heart. Physiologically, the lungs governs gas exchange across ~300 million alveoli. The heart (Cor) is muscular pump in the mediastinum, a little left of midline. Physiologically, the heart drives about 5 L of blood per minute through two circuits. Structurally, the liver (Hepar) comprises largest internal organ, right upper quadrant. Physiologically, the liver governs metabolism, detoxification, bile, plasma proteins. Structurally, the stomach (Gaster) comprises j-shaped reservoir under the diaphragm, left side. Physiologically, the stomach governs acid–pepsin digestion; intrinsic factor for B12.

Clinically, regarding the brain, stroke risk rises with age — remember FAST: face, arms, speech, time. From a diagnostic standpoint, in the thyroid gland, hypothyroidism causes fatigue, weight gain and cold intolerance. In clinical pathology involving the lungs, smoking destroys alveolar walls → emphysema. Medical evaluation of the heart also notes that coronary blockage causes myocardial infarction.

questions.question: Where are the main organs in the female body?
questions.answer: The brain lies in the skull; lungs and heart in the chest; digestive and urinary organs in the abdomen; and uterus, tubes and ovaries in the pelvis. The lungs (Pulmones) is paired thoracic organs flanking the heart. Physiologically, the lungs governs gas exchange across ~300 million alveoli.

questions.answer: No. It is a regional orientation view. Detailed chapters explain deeper pelvic supports, breast tissue, nerves and microscopic layers that a single image cannot resolve.
